documents.title: Academic Integrity (Student Handbook policy)
documents.stance_why: The handbook sets no AI rule of its own; AI use is misconduct only "outside of the bounds established by the instructor and/or course syllabus", and students are told to "consult their instructors", so the decision is delegated to instructors.
documents.summary: A general academic-integrity policy with one passage treating generative AI use beyond instructor or syllabus limits as academic dishonesty and telling students to ask instructors. The rest covers penalties, meetings and appeals for dishonesty in general.

units.why: The sentence says AI use 'outside of the bounds established by the instructor and/or course syllabus' falls under the academic dishonesty designations, so unauthorized AI use is misconduct (P36). It binds students and prohibits out-of-bounds use while they do their work.
units.anchor: done outside of the bounds established by the instructor and/or course syllabus
units.policy: Use of generative AI tools in student-created work outside the bounds set by the instructor and/or course syllabus falls under the academic dishonesty designations.
units.resolution_why: Coder A put phase at during-work, B at when-misuse. The sentence tells students what counts as dishonest while they use AI in their work; sanctions and process come in separate later passages, so during-work fits better than when-misuse. Actor, modality, type and wording agreed.

units.why: The phrase 'bounds established by the instructor and/or course syllabus' leaves the AI rule to each instructor or syllabus; the university sets no AI rule itself, so P04 fits (P36 is used for the neighbouring misconduct unit). It states a general principle about who sets the bounds.
units.anchor: bounds established by the instructor and/or course syllabus
units.policy: What AI use is allowed in student work is determined by the bounds the instructor and/or course syllabus establish.
units.resolution_why: Coder A put phase at before-course, B at general. The passage states a principle about who sets bounds, not an instruction to design a course policy, so general. Both chose P04, actor all, informs, and the same meaning in the policy wording.

units.why: "Students are expected to consult their instructors if they have any questions about the use of AI tools" tells students who are unsure to ask the instructor, which is P10.
units.anchor: Students are expected to consult their instructors if they have any questions

units.why: The handbook says "The instructor decides how to handle violations on a case-by-case basis." Through the AI sentence this covers AI misuse; it is enforcement discretion, not a stated penalty, so the nearest type is P36 with a fit note (P04 is about whether AI is allowed).
units.anchor: The instructor decides how to handle violations on a case-by-case basis.
units.fit_note: Says the instructor, not a fixed rule, decides the response to violations. Not AI-specific; applies to AI misuse through the academic-dishonesty designation.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder B. The source says 'The instructor decides how to handle violations on a case-by-case basis.' It is a real statement of enforcement discretion that reaches AI misuse via the AI sentence, so kept. P36 retained as nearest type with B's fit note; A coded the neighbouring sentence ('effective and educational manner') separately.

units.why: The opening defines integrity as 'ensuring that all ideas and work presented are your own'. It does not mention AI but is the standard the AI sentence imports, and it says submitted work must be the student's own, so P29.
units.anchor: ensuring that all ideas and work presented are your own
units.fit_note: Stated for all academic work, not AI specifically; applies to AI only through the later designation sentence.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A. The source opens with 'ensuring that all ideas and work presented are your own', a standard the AI sentence imports. Real statement, kept with A's P29 and fit note.

units.why: The policy says 'The academic integrity policy applies to all students, undergraduate and graduate, and to scholarly pursuits and research', which sets scope; with the AI sentence it covers AI in research too. P62 is nearest but fits only partly.
units.anchor: applies to all students, undergraduate and graduate, and to scholarly pursuits and research
units.fit_note: A general scope of the integrity policy to research; does not mention AI in research or defer to venue rules.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A. The source says the policy 'applies to all students, undergraduate and graduate, and to scholarly pursuits and research', a scope statement that, with the AI sentence, extends AI rules to research. Kept; P62 is only a partial fit, noted.

units.why: The text says violations will be addressed 'in an effective and educational manner' with the instructor deciding case by case; this covers AI violations since they fall under these designations. The educational framing is P68.
units.anchor: will be addressed in an effective and educational manner
units.frag_start: It is taken seriously at RPI
units.fit_note: Phrase is brief and general to all academic dishonesty, not tied to first offenses or AI.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A. The source says violations 'will be addressed in an effective and educational manner'. It is a real, if brief, statement; kept as P68 with A's fit note. Distinct from B's case-by-case unit, which is a different sentence and rule.

units.why: The handbook lists penalties instructors may impose: "redo the assignment for a reduced grade, assign the student a failing grade for the assignment". They apply to AI misuse because it is classed as academic dishonesty; concrete penalties stated in advance are P37.
units.anchor: redo the assignment for a reduced grade, assign the student a failing grade
units.policy: Within a class, the instructor may require the student to redo the assignment for a reduced grade, assign the student a failing grade for the assignment, assign the student a failing grade for the class, or terminate participation in a research project.
units.fit_note: Not AI-specific; applies to AI misuse through the academic-dishonesty designation.

units.why: "warning, probation, suspension, expulsion" are named disciplinary actions available through the judicial process; they apply to AI misuse by incorporation and are concrete sanctions stated in advance (P37).
units.anchor: warning, probation, suspension, expulsion, and/or alternative actions as agreed on by the student
units.policy: A student may be subject to warning, probation, suspension, expulsion, and/or alternative actions as agreed on by the student and hearing officer(s) if judicial action is pursued by the instructor.
units.fit_note: Not AI-specific; applies to AI misuse through the academic-dishonesty designation.
units.resolution_why: Coder A set actor admin, B set student. The source says 'A student may be subject to any of the following types of disciplinary action', so the sentence is addressed to and affects the student; student kept. Type P37, modality informs and phase agreed.

units.why: The policy bars students found responsible from dropping the course: 'prohibited from dropping a course to avoid the academic penalty'. It is an additional consequence of a finding, so P37.
units.anchor: prohibited from dropping a course to avoid the academic penalty
units.fit_note: A procedural consequence (no drop, no grade-option change) rather than a grade penalty; general to all dishonesty.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A. The source says students found in violation 'are also prohibited from dropping a course to avoid the academic penalty', a real rule binding students. Kept as P37 with A's fit note.

units.why: The instructor "will contact the student(s) about alleged misconduct and schedule a meeting to discuss the allegations", a duty to talk with the student before deciding, which is P57.
units.anchor: will contact the student(s) about alleged misconduct and schedule a meeting
units.fit_note: Not AI-specific; applies to AI misuse through the academic-dishonesty designation.

units.why: The instructor must "allow the student the opportunity to provide their perspective on the situation", a right to respond to allegations, so P64 rather than P57 (talking before escalating).
units.anchor: allow the student the opportunity to provide their perspective on the situation
units.fit_note: Not AI-specific; applies to AI misuse through the academic-dishonesty designation.

units.why: The passage has the instructor review the situation and speak 'with others who might be involved or have knowledge of the situation' before determining the violation, which sets how a finding is reached; nearest type is P69 though no standard of proof is given.
units.anchor: speaking with others who might be involved or have knowledge of the situation
units.frag_end: extent of the violation, if any, by the accused student.
units.fit_note: Describes steps for gathering evidence but states no standard or kinds of evidence insufficient.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A. The source says the instructor determines the violation 'after reviewing the situation and speaking with others who might be involved'. Real procedure; kept as P69 (nearest) with A's fit note, since no evidence standard is stated.

units.why: The written decision must include 'information regarding the student's option to appeal the grade decision', which gives students a route to contest a finding (P64) in cases that include AI.
units.anchor: information regarding the student's option to appeal the grade decision
units.frag_end: time limit in which to do so.
units.fit_note: Concerns notification of appeal rights after the decision, not responding to allegations; general to all dishonesty.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A. The source says the written decision includes 'information regarding the student's option to appeal the grade decision'. Real duty on instructors; kept as P64 with A's fit note.

units.why: Instructors who apply a sanction 'must complete the Academic Integrity Violation Report Form' within a week, and the incident is kept on file 'to track repeat or multiple offenses'. This is an enforcement record rule that fits no listed type, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: must complete the Academic Integrity Violation Report Form on the Dean of Students website
units.frag_end: repeat or multiple offenses by the same student(s).
units.uncovered_note: Instructors must file a violation report with the Dean of Students office, which keeps a record to track repeat offenses.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A. The source says instructors 'must complete the Academic Integrity Violation Report Form' within one week and the Dean of Students keeps a record to track repeat offenses. Real rule with no matching type; UNCOVERED kept.

units.why: The instructor 'can request that formal judicial action be taken against a student in addition to the established academic penalty', with referral to the Director of Student Rights; this escalation route has no matching type, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: the instructor can request that formal judicial action be taken against a student
units.uncovered_note: Instructors may escalate a dishonesty case to formal judicial action on top of the grade penalty.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A. The source says the instructor 'can request that formal judicial action be taken against a student in addition to the established academic penalty'. Real rule with no matching type; UNCOVERED kept.

units.why: The student may "submit a written appeal of an academic penalty to the Department Head", a route to contest a finding; it fits P64 (accused students can respond) though it is an appeal, not an initial response.
units.anchor: a student can submit a written appeal of an academic penalty to the Department Head
units.policy: A student can submit a written appeal of an academic penalty to the Department Head within five Institute business days of being notified of the faculty member's decision.
units.fit_note: Appeal after a finding, not a response to the allegation. Not AI-specific; applies to AI misuse through the academic-dishonesty designation.

documents.title: Generative AI Policy
documents.stance_why: Only a landing page was captured; its purpose, to "establish guidelines for use of generative artificial intelligence (AI)" and "safeguard institutional data", sets no use stance for teaching, so it delegates.
documents.summary: Library landing page for the Generative AI Policy, whose stated purpose is compliance with information security and privacy policies and safeguarding institutional data. The policy document itself was not available.

units.why: The purpose sentence says it will 'establish guidelines for use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) at Rensselaer', an institution-level framework stating purpose and scope (P56). It covers use across the institution, so actor is all.
units.anchor: establish guidelines for use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) at Rensselaer
units.resolution_why: Coder A set actor all, B set admin. The sentence states a purpose of the policy ('to establish guidelines for use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) at Rensselaer') and covers use by anyone at the university, so all. Type P56 agreed.

units.why: The policy aims "to maintain compliance with existing over-arching policies on information security and privacy", i.e. generative AI use must follow existing university policy (P77).
units.anchor: maintain compliance with existing over-arching policies on information security and privacy
units.policy: The generative AI policy exists to maintain compliance with existing over-arching policies on information security and privacy.

units.why: The stated aim "to safeguard institutional data" ties the generative AI policy to data protection (P50). Only the purpose statement was retrievable, so no further rules are coded.
units.anchor: safeguard institutional data
units.policy: The generative AI policy aims to safeguard institutional data.
units.fit_note: States the aim of protecting institutional data only; no instruction about personal data or vetted tools.

notes: Only the purpose statement of the Generative AI Policy was retrievable (PDF not captured). Academic-integrity procedure units are not AI-specific and are coded because the AI sentence incorporates AI misuse into them. Coder A's extra procedural units (own-work definition, scope, educational response, no-drop rule, evidence gathering, appeal notice, report form, judicial escalation) were verified in the source and kept. Topics follow the AGENT_BRIEF starter codes. Syllabus guidance page was inaccessible; no computing-unit policy found; course layer deferred.
